purpose: Reusable safe posture for MIM to turn the base, observe table objects, and begin exploratory object interaction without starting blind.
operator_note: Dave positioned MIM in a safe posture where the base can turn and the hand camera can view table objects.
why_this_matters: This posture gives MIM a local visual frame for object discovery instead of relying only on room-camera guesses.
It supports exploratory base rotation while retaining a close hand-camera view of objects and markers.
It can seed future spatial calibration between base angle, hand-camera image, and object position.
recommended_use: Return to this posture before exploratory object search.
Use small base rotations from this posture while capturing hand-camera frames.
Build a temporary workspace map from changing object positions in the hand camera.
Do not treat marker numbers as fixed; use them only as temporary visual references.
safety_notes: Claw is open in the captured pose.
C12 distance source is live and should be checked before lowering toward table/object contact.
Use slow base movements and capture a frame after each movement.
